request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds are now dated intervals, and a person can have several. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V31__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table (person, from-date, optional to-date) and drops the old `held` column.
- Anyone who was already on hold gets one hold with no dates, so they stay fully held.

**Server**
- `POST …/people/{id}/hold` now takes `{from, to}`. A blank from-date means the sheet's today and a blank to-date means the hold has no end. Each call adds a new hold.
- A hold whose to-date is before its from-date is refused with an error, and nothing is written.
- A successful hold writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`. Releasing is gone.
- The rule for what counts in the live totals is in `Dues.countsLive`. A claim is left out only when it is open (or pending), is not bound by a statement, and its date falls within one of the person's holds (both end dates included). Settled claims and statement-bound claims always count.
- The statement, period and rollup totals all use that one rule, so they change together. When a hold changes the totals, the usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` audit records follow it.

**Front end**
- Each person row now has from and to date inputs and a Hold button.
- The row lists each hold as a `person-hold-line`, and `person-hold` shows yes/no for whether the person has any hold.
- `countsLive` in `core/claims.ts` uses the same rule as the server, so the totals on screen match the stored ones.

Two choices the request didn't spell out:
- **Bound by a statement:** I took this to mean the claim's existing `stated` flag, the same as the "stated" column on screen. That includes a pending claim with the flag set, even though the due figure ignores the statement while the claim is pending.
- **Overlapping holds:** they are allowed, and their effect is the same as one combined hold.
